objects.evidence: The current module imports the actual proximalQuery definition. Its stop branch returns the current point and count one; its continuing branch increments the successful recursive count. Pair equality therefore includes the final counted test.

domains.original: Any real normed vector space and arbitrary real parameters; natural fuels and E-times-natural outputs.

quantifiers.original: Any two successful executions from the same initial point and anchor, regardless of sufficient fuel.

assumptions.original: Only the normed real-space structure and two actual success equations; no positivity, regularity, contraction or termination assumption.
assumptions.reconstructed: Exactly those success equations and typeclasses.
assumptions.evidence: Zero-fuel cases contradict success. For positive fuels the same deterministic residual predicate is used even if eta or eps is nonpositive, so no analytic parameter restriction is necessary.

conclusion.original: Exact equality of returned point and actual gradient-test count.
conclusion.reconstructed: r=s as pairs in E x Nat.
conclusion.evidence: Successful stopping branches give the identical pair (x,1). Nonstopping branches force successful recursive pairs via Option.map_eq_some_iff; induction equates them and congrArg applies the identical count increment. This proves the entire mathematical target.
